cve_summary: drivers/media/video/videobuf-vmalloc.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.24 does not initialize videobuf_mapping data structures, which allows local users to trigger an incorrect count value and videobuf leak via unspecified vectors, a different vulnerability than CVE-2010-5321.
commit_message:
V4L/DVB (6751): V4L: Memory leak!  Fix count in videobuf-vmalloc mmap

This is pretty serious bug.  map->count is never initialized after the
call to kmalloc making the count start at some random trash value.  The
end result is leaking videobufs.

Also, fix up the debug statements to print unsigned values.

Pushed to http://ifup.org/hg/v4l-dvb too

Signed-off-by: Brandon Philips <bphilips@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@infradead.org>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Maps a video buffer to user space memory for a given video buffer queue.

Parameters: 
q (struct videobuf_queue *): Pointer to the video buffer queue to be mapped.
vma (struct vm_area_struct *): Pointer to the virtual memory area structure representing the mapping request.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure (e.g., -EINVAL for invalid parameters, -ENOMEM for memory allocation failure).

Logic: 
The function first checks if the requested memory area is writable and shared. It then searches for the first buffer in the queue that can be mapped, validating its offset. If a valid buffer is found, it allocates a mapping structure and sets up the virtual memory area operations. The function attempts to remap the virtual memory to the physical memory allocated for the buffer. If remapping fails, it stores the virtual memory area for later use. Finally, it logs the mapping details and opens the virtual memory area for access.
"""
